First of the Nemotron HIP stack, on `main` (TensorFold v1.1.0). Review dc595eeb. [fork #28][f28] stacks on it.

## What this changes

The kernel contract (docs/kernel-contract.md) runs on HIP. CONTRIBUTING asks every new or changed GPU kernel to register with it and to post each backend's `SUMMARY` line. Until now the contract's runners were Metal and CUDA only. The stack's HIP kernels register in the pull requests that add them.

- `tf-hip-kernel-contract` (`zig build hip-kernel-contract -Dhip-arch=ARCH`) runs gates 1 to 4 on the GPU for every registered HIP kernel, on the shared core harness (`zig/src/core/contract`). HIP is a backend beside Metal and CUDA. The core gates do not change.
- Each gate has a planted HIP control (`zig/kernels/hip/contract_controls.hip`, built with the kernels): a row max by `fmaxf`, a row sum by `atomicAdd`, a row sum that writes its input, a row sum that loses its tail input, and a dot summed in `__half`. Each must go red at its gate.
- Gate 5 checks every registered HIP launch against gfx1030, gfx1100, gfx1151 and gfx1201, one chip a generation (the caps table's). The records are in `zig/src/core/contract/hip_records.zig`: VGPRs, SGPRs, static LDS, scratch, the `__launch_bounds__` bound and the wave size, for each chip. The checks: threads within the bound and 1,024; wave32; VGPRs a wave within 256; VGPRs a SIMD within its file (1,024 on RDNA2, 1,536 on the others), a workgroup's waves spread over the WGP's four SIMDs; static plus dynamic LDS within 64 KiB.
- `zig build hip-kernel-contract-limits` compiles every kernel group and the controls for the four chips and reads each code object's AMDGPU metadata note (`zig/src/core/contract/hsaco.zig`, msgpack in the offload bundle's ELF). It prints `RECORD` lines and fails on a stale record. No GPU needed. `hip-kernel-contract-objects` installs the code objects.
- On the GPU, gate 5 also checks the device's limits against its chip's row, and each loaded kernel's VGPRs, LDS and thread limit against its record.
- Gate 5's HIP controls: a kernel launched at 512 threads past its `__launch_bounds__(256)`, and 40 KiB of static LDS launched with 32 KiB more. hipcc fits VGPRs to a kernel's bound, so a register overflow shows as a launch past its bound.
- The first registration: the RMS norm rows, a wave a row (`tf_rms_rows`, fp32, fp16 and bf16 out) and a block a row (`rms_kernel`, fp16 and bf16).
- `test-kernel-contract` and `zig build test` run the HIP records against the four chips, the metadata parser and the controls, with no GPU. The runner compiles against stub kernels in `zig build test`.

Shared code: the contract core gains HIP's chip table, launch and usage types and their check (`limits.zig`), and the records and the metadata reader. `zig/build/hip.zig` exposes its group compile for the four chips; the code objects it builds do not change. No production kernel changes.

Outside the contract's files from [fork #49][f49] and the later registrations, `git diff 1e7d79ae 04a707bc` is empty. One change in the rebase: v1.1.0 reads the clock through its platform layer (`sys`), so the moved `nowNs` in `hip_serve/backend.zig` calls `platform.c.clock_gettime`, as v1.1.0's own Qwen3.5 copy did. The receipt on v1.1.0 follows the restacked one. The receipt on 1.0.12 follows as it was; its speeds were measured there.

## What this changes

The serving glue that a HIP family needs beside its forward moves from Qwen3.5's engine into `zig/src/hip_serve`, as generic pieces:

- `backend.zig`: the stream map, the drawn-token ring, the first draws, the held drafts, the prompt pass loop, and the timed verify, keep and draft callbacks;
- `pages.zig` and `snapshots.zig`: page ids, holders and snapshot slots;
- `prefix.zig`: the prompt cache's HIP side over core `prompt_radix` (rank 0 decides, the other ranks apply);
- `protocol.zig`: the tensor-parallel step words, rank 0's sender and the follower loop;
- `costs.zig` (second commit): the lane cost timing at load.

Qwen3.5 now uses these pieces. It keeps its caches, its pool buffers, its batched verify and its draft head. Flash Next keeps its own copies. The next family (Nemotron, later in this stack) uses the same pieces.

Shared code: `hip_serve` and the Qwen3.5 HIP engine. Exactness first: the bits and the behaviour do not change.

Refuses an unsupported HIP fp8 KV-cache request by name before loading, while retaining default behavior.

The proposed gate is strict zero-known nonfinite classes, deterministic/replacement bytes, shape and fp32-sum checks, four-chip launch/resource limits, shared-model regression and source-bound served exactness. Review-head per-PR contracts must be attached before claiming this head is qualified.

**Restacked on the HIP kernel contract.** The stack now starts at [fork #49][f49], which runs the kernel contract on HIP; fork `main` 76aafcf2 (v1.1.0) stays the base. Its commits apply as they were. Outside the contract's files from [fork #49][f49] and the later registrations, `git diff ec1a2d5b 07f27ae5` is empty. The receipt on the restacked head comes first; the earlier receipts follow as they were.

## What this changes

- v1.1.0 adds `--kv-cache fp8`: e4m3 attention caches with a scale a row. CUDA serves it where a family has fp8 caches and refuses it elsewhere. Metal refuses it.
- The native HIP server took the flag and served with 16-bit caches. It said nothing.
- Every HIP family now refuses `--kv-cache fp8` before it loads, on every rank: "--kv-cache fp8 keeps fp8 caches on CUDA; the HIP engines keep 16-bit caches: serve without it".
- Without the flag nothing changes. The check reads only the flag.
- The refusal is temporary. It goes when HIP has fp8 caches.

Shared code: `zig/src/native/hip.zig`. Qwen3.5, Flash Next and (later in this stack) Nemotron all take the check.

## Change and gate

Exposes the routed MoE tile-selection rule for reuse and tests its boundaries.

The proposed gate is strict zero-known nonfinite classes, deterministic/replacement bytes, shape and fp32-sum checks, four-chip launch/resource limits, shared-model regression and source-bound served exactness. Review-head per-PR contracts must be attached before claiming this head is qualified.

The real old-header negative control fails 19 cases: 18 plain-stream and one single relu²; its paired fixture passes. It has zero known findings, five red controls and zero limit problems. Actual review-head NEW / upstream #1098 / upstream #1103 strict checkpoints are complete; the remaining nine planned checkpoints are pending. Prototype results remain separate historical evidence. Nemotron-H's MoE layer on the shared expert plan and routed products (`moe.zig`):

## What this changes

The planned decode walk over the values took all query heads of a KV head on one block. Nemotron-H has 16 query heads a KV head, so a one-row round ran on two blocks. The apply kernel now takes fewer heads a block while the grid is under 128 blocks. It also loads eight values ahead of their sums. A head's sums keep their order, so the bits do not change.

A kernel test runs the planned walk and the one-row paged tile at Nemotron's shape (32 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 128) over 1 to 65,536 keys against float64.

Shared code: `decode/plan.hip` and `launches/plan.zig`, used by every HIP family's lane rounds. Exactness first: Qwen3.5's rounds take the new split (its 35B-A3B has 8 query heads a KV head), and its bits do not change.

The completed 32-hold 8649→cc183 regression, old cold 8k/32k results, prior model/host proofs and 671d NaN-fix receipts remain historical and unchanged. The repository xe-only xpu guard does not establish AMD coverage. Frozen native admission/limits are unchanged. No causal drift explanation, significance, performance threshold, cold-prefill benchmark or full CONTRIBUTING/integration qualification is claimed.

# feat(nemotron): Nemotron-H on the native HIP engine, one GPU: admission, loader, forward and lane backend

**DRAFT / WIP — NOT READY TO LAND.** Tracking proposal: [upstream issue #1081](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1081). These drafts expose the implementation and all available measurements for review; they do not claim completed CONTRIBUTING qualification or request landing.

Tested base: TensorFold v1.1.0 `76aafcf274e60a5e31a59ce145b2f71f7b366e9d`. Observed upstream main: `d1018b318fb51981c4a18f12e40269a4d3ee9713` (96 commits ahead). A read-only merge preflight had no textual conflicts; no integrated tree has been built or runtime-qualified. Review top `1596156e21769324b675ef5e0caae0452f361660` and measured production source `cc18314dce85b0968496b35333bdd8618b2f9227` remain distinct: the complete diff is seven deterministic stress-fixture lines, with production/native/model trees and resource records identical. Any later production optimization needs its own review and revalidation.

Completed evidence ([source-bound proof package](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix)):

- Exact review-head HIP checkpoints: standalone correction 23/23, single relu² [fork #41][f41] 43/43, final paired [fork #46][f46] 49/49, on both gfx1100 and gfx1030; zero failures, known findings and limit problems; all five controls red. Each passed the four-chip resource audit. These are three scheduling checkpoints, not completion of the twelve-head contract plan. Own-head SUMMARY lines appear only in the applicable body below.
- At measured `cc18314d`, HIP kernel tests pass 103/103 on each architecture. All six Qwen decode-logit outputs match reference files byte for byte. Flash Next graphs on/off produce three expected hashes per rig/mode (`6fbb0a3f895f7fa1` W7800 TP2; `349d29968cc98589` V620 TP4), all twelve rank exits zero. Source/binary, input/reference/output hashes and actual loaded-library observations are retained.
- Nemotron checkpoint revision `d9d758fb83953437f7263256b0d96157e2a348b8`: baseline `8649e985` versus measured `cc18314d`, 224-step decode and teacher-forced chat/code/story outputs are finite and byte-identical on W7800 TP2 and V620 TP1; all rank exits zero. These are final-source shared measurements, never per-PR model reruns.
- Production-O3 finite-byte comparisons: 1080 gfx1100 and 540 gfx1030 fixtures, zero byte differences, including 60/24 finite-input NaN-output controls; NaN payloads and signed-zero bytes are compared without canonicalization. The actual-old-header negative has 18 plain and one single relu² numerical failure, zero paired failures, zero known/limit problems, and all five planted controls red.
- Actual review159 host/static checks: Mac 312/312 steps and 4423/4439 tests (16 skipped), plain 220/220; Linux 172/172 steps and 2530/2540 tests (10 skipped), plain 17/17. All 30 commits pass fmt/diff/static checks with zero new lean findings against 503 inherited; HIP host-stub compilation passes.

**Open performance blocker:** measured drafts-on decode throughput decreases versus baseline: V620 code **−32.58%**, chat **−31.50%**; W7800 code **−36.65%**, chat **−34.11%**. These are current measured regressions, not acceptable performance qualification. The full narrow drafts-on/off and 8k/32k A/B is complete, with the regression retained; broader qualification remains pending. Cold-call register/private-memory pressure is being investigated; no unmeasured optimization is claimed fixed.

Before landing: resolve and remeasure that regression; finish the nine remaining planned contract checkpoints and complete the additional CONTRIBUTING lifecycle/context/memory/comparator matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; keep cache/resume, rollback, concurrency, memory and context claims tied to their actual historical/current sources; agree maintainer family/backend and upstream integration gates; qualify any actual integration tree. Historical receipts below remain historical and cannot satisfy new-source gaps. No new CUDA/Metal model, gfx1151/gfx1201 GPU, TP8 or unsupported-format coverage is claimed. No inherited HIP known-finding exemption is accepted. Upstream dependency links above use actual created PR numbers.

Depends on the preceding proposal, “perf(hip): the planned values walk splits a KV head's query heads while its grid is small” ([fork predecessor](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/pull/34)). Actual upstream predecessor: https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/1091.

Published draft source: `6d921a0fde1dba1e14c6d739d3f7f2e64d1ae696` on `nemhip-draft/08-nemotron-engine`. Existing fork review: [source review](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/pull/35); its captured historical head is `bef1ec89d3554ce55baf164538c2d82bf2d5f622`.

## Available raw data and benchmark details

Every completed current proof is linked here: [critical contract logs and exits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/critical_contracts), [O3 finite-byte harness and compiler logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/finite_o3), [actual-old failure and limits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/negative), [kernel/Qwen/Flash model logs and identities](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/models), [Nemotron logits/exits/inputs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/nemotron), [Linux host logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/host), [Mac/static/fixture/source bridge](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/fixture), [benchmark JSON and identity sidecars](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_partial).

- W7800 TP2 code: 255.14 → 161.62 tok/s (−36.65% throughput); prose: 215.29 → 141.85 tok/s (−34.11%).
- V620 TP1 code: 180.17 → 121.46 tok/s (−32.58% throughput); prose: 156.56 → 107.25 tok/s (−31.50%).

Raw requests/replies, source/binary/runtime/checkpoint identities, hashes and reproduction sources are in the benchmark package. The completed full benchmark is added below; this drafts-on subset remains available as its original snapshot. ## Completed full narrow before/after benchmark

[All 32 holds, raw requests/replies, exact input arrays, clients, identity sidecars, controller logs and validation manifests](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_complete). This validates benchmark output consistency, **not acceptable performance or complete CONTRIBUTING qualification**.

- W7800 TP2 drafts on: code 255.14 → 161.62 tok/s (−36.65%); prose 215.29 → 141.85 tok/s (−34.11%).

## What this changes

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B (`nemotron_h`, the MLX affine 4-bit checkpoint with its MTP head) on the native HIP engine, on one GPU:

- Admission reads the config, the index and the MTP file before anything loads. It counts a rank's weight bytes, a stream's keys, values and Mamba state, and the window a card holds. - The loader puts the weights on the device as stored. It does not convert weights in memory. The config, the draft ids and the tensor names are main's (`families/nemotron/config.zig`).
- The forward runs the Mamba-2 mixer ([fork #31][f31]), the MoE layer ([fork #33][f33]) and attention over a page pool.
- The lane backend runs on the `hip_serve` pieces ([fork #29][f29]): MTP drafts, one Mamba snapshot a row so a rejected draft rolls back exactly, and the prompt cache over core `prompt_radix`.
- `tf-nemotron-hip-test` (load, greedy, teacher-forced, window and chunk-cut checks, the replay of a served trace).

## What this changes

Tensor parallelism for the Nemotron HIP engine:

- Each rank holds its cut of the weights: the routed experts, heads and vocabulary by rank, the MTP head whole on rank 0. Every rank sums the shares in fp32 at the same places.
- Rank 0's lane backend sends every prompt pass, chunk, window, keep, page swap and snapshot slot over the link (the `hip_serve` protocol, [fork #29][f29]). A follower runs the same steps on its own shards, so the collectives pair up, and a resumed prompt or a rolled-back draft is exact on every rank.
- The ranks start through `hip.Startup`'s steps over the link. A rank's refusal stops every rank, with its reason.
- `tf-nemotron-hip-test` joins a group for teacher, window, replay and a per-block residual trace.

Family code only: `zig/src/families/nemotron/hip*` and `zig/tests/nemotron_hip`.

## What this changes

- Lane rounds: every stream's window runs in one forward over the round's device plan. A round writes each row's keys and values into its own stream's pages and walks them with the planned decode attention ([fork #34][f34]). A row's bits do not depend on the rows it shares a round with. The Mamba-2 recurrence runs one stream at a time. The MoE layer takes all rows of the round together.
- Lane costs timed at load through `hip_serve/costs.zig` ([fork #29][f29]), as Qwen3.5 does, so the lane core can choose plain rounds over drafted ones.
- A lone stream's rounds replay from graphs cut at their collectives. Every rank votes on a recording (`hip.vote`); one decline runs every rank eagerly. Rounds with several streams run eagerly. `TF_POLICY=graphs=off` keeps every round eager.
- `tf-nemotron-hip-test decode`: the decode path teacher-forced a row at a time, for a reference to score.

Family code only: `zig/src/families/nemotron/hip*` and `zig/tests/nemotron_hip`.

# perf(nemotron): HIP prompts in 2048-row chunks, so the routed experts get enough rows a tile

**DRAFT / WIP — NOT READY TO LAND.** Tracking proposal: [upstream issue #1081](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1081). These drafts expose the implementation and all available measurements for review; they do not claim completed CONTRIBUTING qualification or request landing.

Cold-call register/private-memory pressure is being investigated; no unmeasured optimization is claimed fixed.

Before landing: resolve and remeasure that regression; finish the nine remaining planned contract checkpoints and complete the additional CONTRIBUTING lifecycle/context/memory/comparator matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; keep cache/resume, rollback, concurrency, memory and context claims tied to their actual historical/current sources; agree maintainer family/backend and upstream integration gates; qualify any actual integration tree. No inherited HIP known-finding exemption is accepted. Upstream dependency links above use actual created PR numbers.

## Available raw data and benchmark details

Every completed current proof is linked here: [critical contract logs and exits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/critical_contracts), [O3 finite-byte harness and compiler logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/finite_o3), [actual-old failure and limits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/negative), [kernel/Qwen/Flash model logs and identities](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/models), [Nemotron logits/exits/inputs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/nemotron), [Linux host logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/host), [Mac/static/fixture/source bridge](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/fixture), [benchmark JSON and identity sidecars](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_partial).

- W7800 TP2 code: 255.14 → 161.62 tok/s (−36.65% throughput); prose: 215.29 → 141.85 tok/s (−34.11%).
- V620 TP1 code: 180.17 → 121.46 tok/s (−32.58% throughput); prose: 156.56 → 107.25 tok/s (−31.50%).

The completed full benchmark is added below; this drafts-on subset remains available as its original snapshot. ## What this changes

- Nemotron on HIP now runs prompts in 2,048-row chunks. Before, it ran them in 512-row chunks.
- The routed experts get more rows a tile. A 512-row chunk gives each expert about 24 rows, in a tile of 128 rows. The routed fc1 and fc2 products took about half of a prefill.
- The prompt path does not change. Every prompt row runs on the prefill kernels at any row count, so its bits do not depend on where a chunk ends. The lane rounds, the decode path and the prompt cache do not change.
- The scratch arena stays at 2 GiB. A 2,048-row chunk uses 1.16 GiB of it at tp 1. Admission, the streams and the prompt cache get the same bytes as before.
- `tf-nemotron-hip-test teacher` uses the engine's chunk by default.

Family code only: `zig/src/families/nemotron/hip/engine.zig` and `zig/tests/nemotron_hip/gen.zig`. The change is one constant. It has no new host logic to test, so it adds no host test.

# perf(hip): the residual add and the RMS norm in one launch, the Nemotron MoE sum among its inputs

**DRAFT / WIP — NOT READY TO LAND.** Tracking proposal: [upstream issue #1081](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1081). These drafts expose the implementation and all available measurements for review; they do not claim completed CONTRIBUTING qualification or request landing.

Tested base: TensorFold v1.1.0 `76aafcf274e60a5e31a59ce145b2f71f7b366e9d`. Observed upstream main: `d1018b318fb51981c4a18f12e40269a4d3ee9713` (96 commits ahead). Review top `1596156e21769324b675ef5e0caae0452f361660` and measured production source `cc18314dce85b0968496b35333bdd8618b2f9227` remain distinct: the complete diff is seven deterministic stress-fixture lines, with production/native/model trees and resource records identical. Any later production optimization needs its own review and revalidation.

Completed evidence ([source-bound proof package](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix)):

- Exact review-head HIP checkpoints: standalone correction 23/23, single relu² [fork #41][f41] 43/43, final paired [fork #46][f46] 49/49, on both gfx1100 and gfx1030; zero failures, known findings and limit problems; all five controls red. - At measured `cc18314d`, HIP kernel tests pass 103/103 on each architecture. All six Qwen decode-logit outputs match reference files byte for byte. Flash Next graphs on/off produce three expected hashes per rig/mode (`6fbb0a3f895f7fa1` W7800 TP2; `349d29968cc98589` V620 TP4), all twelve rank exits zero. Source/binary, input/reference/output hashes and actual loaded-library observations are retained.
- Nemotron checkpoint revision `d9d758fb83953437f7263256b0d96157e2a348b8`: baseline `8649e985` versus measured `cc18314d`, 224-step decode and teacher-forced chat/code/story outputs are finite and byte-identical on W7800 TP2 and V620 TP1; all rank exits zero. These are final-source shared measurements, never per-PR model reruns.
- Production-O3 finite-byte comparisons: 1080 gfx1100 and 540 gfx1030 fixtures, zero byte differences, including 60/24 finite-input NaN-output controls; NaN payloads and signed-zero bytes are compared without canonicalization. The actual-old-header negative has 18 plain and one single relu² numerical failure, zero paired failures, zero known/limit problems, and all five planted controls red.
- Actual review159 host/static checks: Mac 312/312 steps and 4423/4439 tests (16 skipped), plain 220/220; Linux 172/172 steps and 2530/2540 tests (10 skipped), plain 17/17. All 30 commits pass fmt/diff/static checks with zero new lean findings against 503 inherited; HIP host-stub compilation passes.

**Open performance blocker:** measured drafts-on decode throughput decreases versus baseline: V620 code **−32.58%**, chat **−31.50%**; W7800 code **−36.65%**, chat **−34.11%**. These are current measured regressions, not acceptable performance qualification. The full narrow drafts-on/off and 8k/32k A/B is complete, with the regression retained; broader qualification remains pending. Cold-call register/private-memory pressure is being investigated; no unmeasured optimization is claimed fixed.

Before landing: resolve and remeasure that regression; finish the nine remaining planned contract checkpoints and complete the additional CONTRIBUTING lifecycle/context/memory/comparator matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; keep cache/resume, rollback, concurrency, memory and context claims tied to their actual historical/current sources; agree maintainer family/backend and upstream integration gates; qualify any actual integration tree. No inherited HIP known-finding exemption is accepted. Upstream dependency links above use actual created PR numbers.

Every completed current proof is linked here: [critical contract logs and exits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/critical_contracts), [O3 finite-byte harness and compiler logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/finite_o3), [actual-old failure and limits](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/negative), [kernel/Qwen/Flash model logs and identities](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/models), [Nemotron logits/exits/inputs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/nemotron), [Linux host logs](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/host), [Mac/static/fixture/source bridge](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/fixture), [benchmark JSON and identity sidecars](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_partial).

The completed full benchmark is added below; this drafts-on subset remains available as its original snapshot. ## Completed full narrow before/after benchmark

[All 32 holds, raw requests/replies, exact input arrays, clients, identity sidecars, controller logs and validation manifests](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_complete). All eight condition quartets validate complete reply/token equality; cold cached-token counts are zero. This validates benchmark output consistency, **not acceptable performance or complete CONTRIBUTING qualification**.

- W7800 TP2 drafts on: code 255.14 → 161.62 tok/s (−36.65%); prose 215.29 → 141.85 tok/s (−34.11%).
- W7800 TP2 drafts off: code 148.33 → 72.73 tok/s (−50.97%); prose 146.65 → 71.78 tok/s (−51.05%).

- Cold 8k first TTFT: W7800 1.733 → 1.733 s (+0.04%); V620 3.464 → 3.462 s (−0.05%).
- Cold 32k first TTFT: W7800 9.151 → 8.973 s (−1.94%); V620 17.495 → 17.458 s (−0.21%). W7800 baseline holds drifted 8.900 → 9.402 s; the −1.94% mean does not establish a prefill speedup. Full hold-order timings and all three cold request timings are retained.

Decode percentages describe throughput change; TTFT percentages describe elapsed-time change. Rates above are rounded; exact underlying values are in summary.json. The decode regression remains open. Additional 2k/64k/applicable-long-context, memory/comparator and lifecycle/state requirements remain pending, as does actual upstream integration.

## Change and gate

Fuses the residual add and RMS normalization, including the Nemotron MoE sum input, with separate operations as references.

The proposed gate is strict zero-known nonfinite classes, deterministic/replacement bytes, shape and fp32-sum checks, four-chip launch/resource limits, shared-model regression and source-bound served exactness. Review-head per-PR contracts must be attached before claiming this head is qualified.

## Completed evidence, with source boundaries

At measured production source `cc18314d`, production-O3 old/new comparisons pass 1080 gfx1100 and 540 gfx1030 finite fixtures with zero byte differences, including finite-input NaN payloads. Review top `1596156e` differs only by seven stress-fixture lines; production trees and resource records are identical. Full review-top Mac/Linux host checks, all 30 static checks and the HIP host stub have passed. Both architecture kernel suites pass 103/103; all six Qwen decode outputs match byte for byte and Flash Next graphs on/off match all twelve expected hashes at measured `cc18314d`. Current Nemotron decode and chat/code/story teacher outputs also match baseline bytes on both rigs, as detailed in the WIP block. These shared results are not runtime reruns at every proposal head.

The real old-header negative control fails 19 cases: 18 plain-stream and one single relu²; its paired fixture passes. It has zero known findings, five red controls and zero limit problems. Actual review-head NEW / upstream #1098 / upstream #1103 strict checkpoints are complete; the remaining nine planned checkpoints are pending. Prototype results remain separate historical evidence. No HIP known-finding exception is accepted.

## Pending before landing

- Complete the remaining nine planned exact-head contract checkpoints. Shared critical-checkpoint results do not imply this proposal has an own-head current run; see the explicit scope below.
- Shared Qwen/Flash Next and Nemotron correctness checks are complete at measured cc18314d. Resolve the measured decode regression and complete the additional qualification matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; retain exact source/binary identities and historical timings separately.

## What this changes

- `tf_add_rms` adds a row to the residual and norms the new row in one launch. It adds as `tf_add` does: an activation row, an fp32 rank sum as `tf_add_wide` does, or a MoE layer's expert rows summed as `tf_nemo_combine` sums them. Then it norms the row as `tf_rms` does.
- One block of 1024 threads takes a row. Each element's arithmetic is the replaced launches'. The norm's sum keeps `rms_kernel`'s order: one wave, lane l over the elements l, l + 32, ..., then the same xor tree. So the bits are those of the launches it replaces.
- `ops.residualRms` and `residualMoeRms` take it for rows of 1,025 to 8,192 values while the merged launches are on. Otherwise they run the launches it replaces. `reduce.residualNorm` sums the ranks' shares first, as `residual` does.
- `moe_nemotron.expertRows` returns a layer's expert rows, weights and shared row before their sum. `run` sums them as before, so a caller of `run` gets the same launches.
- No family calls the new op in this PR. [fork #44][f44] uses it.

## What this changes

- `tf_mamba_conv_window` runs `tf_mamba_conv` over a window's rows, and `tf_mamba_dt` in the blocks past the conv's. It keeps the conv tail after each row but the last in that row's snapshot slot.
- `tf_mamba_scan_snap` walks the rows as `tf_mamba_scan` does and keeps each state but the last in its slot. A lone row takes `tf_mamba_scan` itself. `tf_mamba_gnorm` follows.
- `ops.mambaWindow` gives the bits of the four launches a row at a time with the state copied out after each row. Slot 0 is not written: the caller keeps the state before the window if it needs it.
- No family calls it in this PR. [fork #44][f44] uses it.

Shared code: `recurrence/mamba.hip`, `launches/mamba.zig`, `ops/mamba.zig`, `launches.zig`, `ops/ops.zig`. The existing Mamba kernels are unchanged. Only Nemotron uses them.

## What this changes

- `affine_dot2_stream_relu2` is the decode stream tile with `tf_nemo_relu2` as its epilogue. It rounds the sum to the activation type, takes its relu, squares it in fp32 and rounds again. The fp32 product followed by `tf_nemo_relu2` gives the same bits.
- `projectRelu2` and `projectRoutedRelu2` take it where the registry picks the stream tile for the product. Otherwise they return false and launch nothing.
- `moe_nemotron` takes it for the routed fc1 and the shared up of a one-row layer. Layers of more rows keep the relu^2 launches: there the epilogue ran slower (lane costs of 2 and 3 rows rose by 0.2 ms).
- The existing stream tiles are unchanged, and the registry's choice does not change.

## What this changes

- `tf_argmax_part` takes the best of each 1,024-value part of a row on its own block. `tf_argmax_join` takes the best of those.
- `tf_argmax`'s order is total: a NaN first, then the larger value, then the lower index. So the best of the parts' bests is `tf_argmax`'s pick, whatever the parts are.
- `ops.argmaxRows` takes the parts for rows of 2,048 values and more while the merged launches are on. That is every HIP family's greedy draw and Nemotron's draft head.

Shared code: `ops/draw.hpp`, `launches/draw.zig`, `ops/draw.zig`, `launches.zig`. This changes Qwen3.5's and Flash Next's greedy draws: the picks are the same, as the decode logits, lanes and hashes below show.

## What this changes

Family code only: `zig/src/families/nemotron/hip/` and `zig/tests/nemotron_hip/gen.zig`. Each commit fuses launches of Nemotron's HIP decode on the shared kernels of [fork #39][f39] to [fork #43][f43]:

- 8caabbc4: the attention's q, k and v run as one grouped stream-tile launch (`ops.projectGroup`). A column's sum order depends on K alone, so the bits are those of three launches. A prompt pass keeps its three launches.
- b5de55c8: every block's residual add and the next block's input norm run as one launch (`hip.reduce.residualNorm`), the final norm after the last block too, and the MTP head's norms after its attention and MoE.
- 629c91d5: on one rank, a MoE block's expert rows, weights and shared row go straight to the residual's launch (`residualMoeRms`), so `tf_nemo_combine` and `tf_add` run inside it. Under tensor parallelism the ranks' fp32 shares are summed first, as before.
- 59789d65: a lane round runs a stream's Mamba rows through `ops.mambaWindow`: three launches for the window instead of four a row. Each row's state but the last goes to its snapshot slot from inside the kernels, so no state copy runs. Slot 0, the state before the window, is no longer kept: a keep holds the pending row at least (`keepRows` now refuses zero rows), so nothing read it. The test tool's rollback check runs for windows of three rows or more.
- b86e111b: Nemotron's attention has no RoPE, so q and the keys go to the planned walk as they are and its rows come back in the activation type: three casts fewer an attention layer.

# perf(hip): the planned decode walk in one launch a query head for spans up to 4096 keys

**DRAFT / WIP — NOT READY TO LAND.** Tracking proposal: [upstream issue #1081](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1081). These drafts expose the implementation and all available measurements for review; they do not claim completed CONTRIBUTING qualification or request landing.

Completed evidence ([source-bound proof package](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix)):

- Production-O3 finite-byte comparisons: 1080 gfx1100 and 540 gfx1030 fixtures, zero byte differences, including 60/24 finite-input NaN-output controls; NaN payloads and signed-zero bytes are compared without canonicalization. Cold-call register/private-memory pressure is being investigated; no unmeasured optimization is claimed fixed.

Before landing: resolve and remeasure that regression; finish the nine remaining planned contract checkpoints and complete the additional CONTRIBUTING lifecycle/context/memory/comparator matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; keep cache/resume, rollback, concurrency, memory and context claims tied to their actual historical/current sources; agree maintainer family/backend and upstream integration gates; qualify any actual integration tree. ## Completed full narrow before/after benchmark

[All 32 holds, raw requests/replies, exact input arrays, clients, identity sidecars, controller logs and validation manifests](https://github.com/BlivionIaG/TensorFold/tree/981188928345191165477d530a068e01f3ba4a17/receipts/nemotron-hip/streamfix/ab_complete). All eight condition quartets validate complete reply/token equality; cold cached-token counts are zero. This validates benchmark output consistency, **not acceptable performance or complete CONTRIBUTING qualification**.

- W7800 TP2 drafts on: code 255.14 → 161.62 tok/s (−36.65%); prose 215.29 → 141.85 tok/s (−34.11%).
- W7800 TP2 drafts off: code 148.33 → 72.73 tok/s (−50.97%); prose 146.65 → 71.78 tok/s (−51.05%).

- Cold 32k first TTFT: W7800 9.151 → 8.973 s (−1.94%); V620 17.495 → 17.458 s (−0.21%). W7800 baseline holds drifted 8.900 → 9.402 s; the −1.94% mean does not establish a prefill speedup. Full hold-order timings and all three cold request timings are retained.

Decode percentages describe throughput change; TTFT percentages describe elapsed-time change. Rates above are rounded; exact underlying values are in summary.json. The decode regression remains open. Additional 2k/64k/applicable-long-context, memory/comparator and lifecycle/state requirements remain pending, as does actual upstream integration.

## Change and gate

Runs the planned decode attention walk in one launch per query head for spans up to 4096 keys.

The proposed gate is strict zero-known nonfinite classes, deterministic/replacement bytes, shape and fp32-sum checks, four-chip launch/resource limits, shared-model regression and source-bound served exactness. Review-head per-PR contracts must be attached before claiming this head is qualified.

## Completed evidence, with source boundaries

At measured production source `cc18314d`, production-O3 old/new comparisons pass 1080 gfx1100 and 540 gfx1030 finite fixtures with zero byte differences, including finite-input NaN payloads. Review top `1596156e` differs only by seven stress-fixture lines; production trees and resource records are identical. Full review-top Mac/Linux host checks, all 30 static checks and the HIP host stub have passed. Both architecture kernel suites pass 103/103; all six Qwen decode outputs match byte for byte and Flash Next graphs on/off match all twelve expected hashes at measured `cc18314d`. Current Nemotron decode and chat/code/story teacher outputs also match baseline bytes on both rigs, as detailed in the WIP block. These shared results are not runtime reruns at every proposal head.

The real old-header negative control fails 19 cases: 18 plain-stream and one single relu²; its paired fixture passes. It has zero known findings, five red controls and zero limit problems. Actual review-head NEW / upstream #1098 / upstream #1103 strict checkpoints are complete; the remaining nine planned checkpoints are pending. Prototype results remain separate historical evidence. No HIP known-finding exception is accepted.

## Pending before landing

- Complete the remaining nine planned exact-head contract checkpoints. Shared critical-checkpoint results do not imply this proposal has an own-head current run; see the explicit scope below.
- Shared Qwen/Flash Next and Nemotron correctness checks are complete at measured cc18314d. Resolve the measured decode regression and complete the additional qualification matrix beyond the completed narrow A/B; retain exact source/binary identities and historical timings separately.
- Agree the family gate, review split and upstream integration strategy with the maintainer. Any explicit deferral remains visible rather than silently treated as complete.

## What this changes

- `tf_plan_attend_f16` and `_bf16` walk one row's query head over its keys in one block of 1,024 threads. They read q and write the row in the activation type, as [fork #42][f42]'s walk does.
- The block runs the four launches' code in turn: `plan_score_body`'s scores (a wave a key), `tf_softmax_stats`' max and sum on the first 256 threads, `plan_apply_body`'s 128-key tiles eight at a time, and `tf_sum_partials`' sum of the tiles in order. Each sum keeps its kernel's order, so the bits are those of the four launches.
- `ops.causalAct` takes it for spans up to 4,096 keys and heads up to 128 wide while the merged launches are on. Longer spans keep the four launches.
- Nemotron's decode takes it through `causalAct` ([fork #44][f44]). No family file changes.

Shared code: `decode/plan.hip`, `launches/plan.zig`, `ops/plan.zig`, `launches.zig`. Only Nemotron calls `causalAct`. Qwen3.5 and Flash Next do not.

## Historical tracker record

The prior issue text follows with its original measured source identities; its current-status wording applies to that captured source.

Following [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), I would like to agree on the scope and qualification gate before opening the Nemotron family PRs.

The proposed addition is **Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B (`nemotron_h`) on the existing native HIP backend**, using the [MLX affine 4-bit, group-64 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/TensorFold/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit), including its MTP head. It reuses the shared lane core, loader, cache, graph and RCCL paths. Mamba-2 keeps a sequential fp32 recurrence. Metal/CUDA implementation files are unchanged; unsupported checkpoint formats and HIP options are refused by name.

This follows the [small-slice/shared-runtime approach discussed on #491](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/491#issuecomment-6096495227). It does not propose a second HIP runtime or family scheduler.
